transport: A train to 190th St, then a short walk; or 1 train to 191st St
verify_notes: Fort Tryon Park Trust (fetched): elms described as 100+ years old, planted widely in the early 1900s; the Trust pays to inoculate 48 elms against Dutch elm disease every other year; many original elms already died. The most-cited tree is the large elm at the northern end of the Stan Michels Promenade whose low branches reach into the Heather Garden (the Trust's search-snippet text says the Heather Garden opened 1935, promenade lined with American elms). No source names a single tree or gives its size. The two biggest American elms in the park's forestry points are 59 in and 54 in about 70 m apart along the promenade, but I could not prove which is the 'northern end' elm, so the pin is one of them and approximate; girth_cm uses 59 in diameter x pi. Age 'over a century' is the Trust's 100+ year-old wording for the stock, not a date for this tree. Entry is a small group of two. Flagged.
